analysis.title: Prime Services Weekly Report
key_insights: The GS Equity Fundamental L/S Performance Estimate fell -0.45% between 9/25 and 10/1 versus MSCI World TR at -0.67%. The move was driven almost entirely by beta, and alpha finished roughly flat.
The GS Equity Systematic L/S Performance Estimate rose +1.14% over the same period. Alpha contributed +1.27% on short side gains, partly offset by beta of -0.13%.

Overall book gross leverage was unchanged at 308.0% (55th percentile 1-year). Net leverage was unchanged at 77.4% (29th percentile 1-year). The L/S ratio was unchanged at 1.671 (28th percentile 1-year).
Fundamental L/S gross leverage fell 1.7 pts to 206.2% (21st percentile 1-year). Net leverage fell 2.1 pts to 53.0% (7th percentile 1-year).
Global equities were net bought (+0.7 SDs 1-year), with long buys outpacing short sales 2.7 to 1. All major regions except EM Asia were net bought, led in dollar terms by Europe and North America.
Macro Products were net bought at the fastest pace in 2 months, driven by short covers and to a lesser extent long buys. Single Stocks were net sold for a 3rd straight week, driven by short sales.
Health Care, Utilities and Energy were the most dollar net bought global sectors. Comm Svcs, Cons Disc and Info Tech were the most net sold.

Health Care was by far the most dollar net bought sector and saw the largest % net buying in over 6 months, driven by short covers in North America and long buys in Europe. All subsectors except Health Care Tech were net bought, led by Biotech, Health Care Equipment & Supplies and Pharmaceuticals.
The Prime book is over-weight Health Care versus MSCI World by +5.5% (46th percentile 1-year, 89th percentile 5-year). Gross/net allocation to Health Care is 11.5%/13.8%.

Info Tech saw the largest % net selling in 6 weeks, driven by long sales in EM Asia and Europe. Selling in Semis & Semi Equipment, and to a lesser extent IT Services and Tech Hardware, outpaced buying in Software.
The Prime book is under-weight Info Tech versus MSCI World by -6.0%. Gross/net allocation to Info Tech is 23.5%/27.6%, in the 79th percentile 1-year and 96th percentile 5-year.

The largest regional flow changes were in Europe, with long buys of +1.56 SDs and short covers of +0.91 SDs. The largest sector flow changes were Utilities long buys of +2.40 SDs and Real Estate short sales of -2.46 SDs.

sector_views.rationale: Prime book is over-weight MSCI World by +5.5% after the largest % net buying in over 6 months, driven by short covers in North America and long buys in Europe.
Prime book is under-weight MSCI World by -6.0% after the largest % net selling in 6 weeks, led by long sales in EM Asia and Europe, particularly in Semis & Semi Equipment.
Long buys of +2.40 SDs were the largest sector flow change of the week.
Short sales of -2.46 SDs were the largest short-side sector flow change of the week.

vol_and_positioning: Overall book gross leverage 308.0% (55th percentile 1-year, 85th 3-year, 91st 5-year). Net leverage 77.4% (29th percentile 1-year). L/S ratio 1.671 (28th percentile 1-year).
Fundamental L/S gross leverage 206.2% (21st percentile 1-year) and net leverage 53.0% (7th percentile 1-year), after falling 1.7 pts and 2.1 pts respectively.
Trailing 12-month range for overall book gross leverage is 282.7% to 322.9% (average 303.5%). Net leverage ranges 69.2% to 82.9% (average 78.6%).

Global equities net bought at +0.7 SDs with long buys outpacing short sales 2.7 to 1. Single Stocks were net sold for a 3rd straight week on short sales, while Macro Products saw the fastest net buying in 2 months on short covers.
VIX level 16.39 with a week-over-week change of +4.6%. SPX realized correlation 11.0% (+2.0 pp).
